script.base: Spread and total are not in the pack, so this is form-only. KC's clearest edge is Kenneth Walker (65 carries, 360 rush yards, 5.54 YPC, 120.0 rush yards/game) into an LV run defense allowing 4.47 YPC and 8 runs of 10+. KC also has two high-volume pass options (Travis Kelce 18 targets/231 rec yards; Rashee Rice 17/190) while LV's run game is volume without efficiency (Ashton Jeanty 63/206, 3.27 YPC) and KC allows only 3.90 YPC and 5 passes of 20+ on 99 attempts. Base script: KC controls into the second half, Walker stays near 18-22 carries, Kelce works the middle on about 5-6 targets, and LV is pushed toward checkdowns rather than explosives.
script.flip1: KC jumps ahead early and clocks it. Walker rush overs are helped; Kelce and Rice receiving yards stall after halftime, so pass-catcher overs are script-dependent on this flip.
script.flip2: LV hangs around or leads and KC throws to chase. Walker carries fall toward the mid-teens and the rush over is at risk; Kelce/Rice overs benefit. LV still is unlikely to rip explosives given KC's 5/99 rate.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Walker: LV sells out to the run, his 5.54 YPC regresses toward something under 4.0, and a chase script cuts him to about 15 carries, so 15 times 4.0 is 60 and 86.5 never threatens; the 360 yards may also be one spike game the aggregate hides. Kelce: the 231 yards are one long-YAC game, his true rate is near 40, LV's middle 9.83 YPA is 12 attempts of noise, and a KC clock-kill after an early lead holds him under 4 targets and under 47.5. That counter is real on Kelce (lean, script-dependent) and weaker on Walker, whose 65-carry role still clears 86.5 at LV's own 4.47 YPC if carries stay near 20.
slip_story: One story: KC's offense functions and controls, not a shootout and not a total (total not in pack). Anchor is Kenneth Walker rush yards over in the lead/clock script; Travis Kelce receiving yards over belongs only while KC is still throwing, and is tagged script-dependent on flip 1 (early KC lead, pure run). Do not add LV deep overs (Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor) that need explosives KC has not allowed, and do not add Ashton Jeanty rush under — his 68.7 rush yards/game is above 59, so that under needs the opposite of his own volume.
